title: POC Quant Pilot - KPI Tuning Sync (Week 4)
summary: Week 4 sync covering quantization results across INT8 and experimental FP8 runs. Team reviewed quality deltas on instruction-following prompts, latency/throughput improvements, identified a small repeat/hallucination regression on a subset of prompts, agreed on calibration expansion and a final benchmark run. Action items assigned for calibration, additional evals, and updating fallback rules.

Customer to provide 300 golden prompts covering critical intents by 2025-07-11
SE to add FP8 fallback route to canary policy and test in staging by 2025-07-15
action_items: Priya Natarajan - run expanded calibration and post results to shared benchmark sheet - due 2025-07-14
Diego Fernandez - share production traffic subset (anonymized) for calibration sampling - due 2025-07-11
Lina Park - deliver 300 golden prompts and success criteria doc - due 2025-07-11

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-08 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Marco Liu (Redwood SE), Jared Mills (Nimble Analytics), Sara Okoye (Nimble ML), Diego Fernandez (Nimble SRE), Lina Park (Nimble DS)

[00:00] Alex Carter: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the week four tune and kpi sync for the quant pilot. quick roll call?
[00:08] Jared Mills: Jared here, plus Sara and Diego and Lina, all good.
[00:12] Priya Natarajan: Priya from Redwood, Marco and Alex on the line as well. we'll jump right into the results that we posted to the benchmark sheet.
[00:22] Alex Carter: quick agenda — perf deltas (latency/throughput), quality deltas (instruction-following/regression hits), calibration notes, and next steps. any additions?
[00:30] Sara Okoye: small ask — can we call out hallucination cases separately? those are highest risk for us.
[00:35] Priya Natarajan: noted. we'll highlight hallucination/repeat cases and suggested mitigations.

[02:10] Marco Liu: ok so first slide, posted numbers are median p95 latency per inference at 1024 context for INT8 vs FP16 baseline and a FP8 experimental run. INT8 gave ~2.6x token throughput improvement and p95 latency reduced from 380ms to about 150ms under our batching shape. FP8 experiments are promising — about 3.1x throughput vs baseline but slightly more variance on edge cases.
[02:45] Diego Fernandez: can you quantify variance? we care about tail a lot.
[02:50] Marco Liu: yes p99 for INT8 was 420ms, for FP8 p99 hit 610ms on a small number of requests where we saw cache refill + outlier activations. so FP8 improves average but has a heavier tail in our current quant recipe.

[05:00] Priya Natarajan: switching to quality now — we ran our validation set (3k prompts) plus a 400 prompt instruction-heavy golden set you supplied. INT8 quality overall stayed within our 1.5% semantic sim delta (embedding cosine) and Rouge-L remained within noise for most tasks. FP8 showed occasionally higher delta — about 3-6% degradation on a small subset of persona and long-form summarization prompts.
[05:40] Lina Park: that 3-6% — was that consistent across seeds or concentrated?
[05:44] Priya Natarajan: it clustered — looks concentrated on longer context and on prompts with nested instructions (multi-step). we traced to layer-activation outliers in 2 middle transformer blocks, which FP8 quantization amplifies.

[07:20] Jared Mills: any examples we can see now?
[07:24] Priya Natarajan: yes shared two transcripts in the sheet — Example A shows repetition on step 2 of the instruction, Example B has an extra hallucinated entity in the summary. these were flagged by your golden prompts.
[07:40] Sara Okoye: hmm, that repetition is concerning. is this fixable with calibration or do we need retraining?
[07:48] Marco Liu: initial mitigation is improved calibration (larger calibration set and per-channel min/max stats), activation clipping on high-variance layers, or using hybrid strategy: INT8 for most layers and FP16/FP32 for the two offending layers (mixed quant).

[10:05] Diego Fernandez: mixed quant seems appealing but more complex to ops. what is the memory/cost trade?
[10:12] Priya Natarajan: mixed quant still gives majority of size savings; in our tests mixed (2 layers in FP16) yields ~2.2x throughput vs baseline and p95 ~180ms, so slightly worse than full INT8 but safer on quality. cost delta is small versus full FP16 hosting.

[12:30] Alex Carter: also note Redwood runtime can apply runtime fallback: route requests that match critical intent to FP16 variant while running background traffic on quantized variant — we showed sample routing rules in the playbook.
[12:45] Sara Okoye: latency SLA for checkout flow is strict, but some internal analytics queries are fine with higher latency. we should map intents.

[15:00] Priya Natarajan: on calibration: we expanded the calibration set from 512 to 2048 samples for this run, but we think 8k samples will smooth some of the outlier activations. also using a stratified sample covering long-form, nested instructions, persona prompts.
[15:24] Lina Park: we'll provide the 300 golden blocker prompts tonight, which are the highest-risk cases.

[18:10] Marco Liu: one more perf nuance — KV cache size for longer contexts increased memory pressure in FP8 because quantized kernels currently allocate slightly different transient buffers. we're working with runtime team to tighten that.
[18:30] Diego Fernandez: any risk to production? we want to try in staging first.
[18:35] Alex Carter: absolutely, we'll run a staging canary with 5% traffic and the fallback to FP16 if error or semantic-sim drop exceeds threshold.

[21:00] Jared Mills: what's our observed hallucination rate delta? numbers please.
[21:06] Priya Natarajan: baseline hallucination on golden set ~2.2% of outputs flagged. INT8 changed that to 2.6% (so +0.4% absolute) — FP8 was 3.5% (+1.3% absolute). those are concentrated on instructions requiring multi-step state.
[21:30] Sara Okoye: that's within our tolerance for non-critical paths but not for checkout or user-facing responses.

[24:10] Marco Liu: proposed mitigations recap: expanded calibration to 8k, per-channel quantization stats, activation clipping, and mixed-precision for two mid-block layers. also a routing rule for critical intents to default FP16.

[26:00] Priya Natarajan: we ran a quick ablation — activation clipping reduced hallucination delta by ~0.5% for FP8 but cost is slight quality hit on exact numeric outputs. need more eval.

[28:30] Diego Fernandez: curious about the experience on bursty traffic — does latency tail worsen if cache misses coincide?
[28:36] Marco Liu: yes p99 increases when cache refill occurs simultaneously; we saw p99 spikes to 900ms in synthetic bursts for FP8; INT8 stayed below 520ms. so FP8 is more sensitive to cache refill patterns right now.

[31:10] Alex Carter: ok decision paths — for stage: run expanded calibration and try mixed-precision recipe; staging canary of 5% with routing for critical intents to FP16; collect production-like traces for two weeks; if hallucination delta stays <=0.6% absolute above baseline, expand to 25% traffic.

[33:00] Lina Park: question about tooling — can we tag spans in traces with quant variant? need to correlate errors with model variant.
[33:08] Priya Natarajan: yes we can emit variant tags and include token-level latency breakdown in the trace. we'll enable that for the canary.

[35:40] Marco Liu: also posted a small script for offline evaluation to replay anonymized requests against both variants and compute semantic sim, rouge, and hallucination flags. we recommend running that nightly during the pilot.
[36:00] Jared Mills: we'll run it for a week and return results.

[38:10] Alex Carter: pricing/ops note — FP8 experimental pricing add-on is about +8% on unit cost vs INT8 due to kernel maintenance and monitoring. Alex to send formal delta.
[38:25] Alex Carter: i'll send SOW update and price delta later today.

[40:00] Priya Natarajan: quick risks: FP8 tail spikes and hallucination clusters on nested instructions — mitigations enumerated.
[41:00] Sara Okoye: thanks, want to ensure we keep a rollback plan.
[41:10] Marco Liu: rollback is immediate via routing policy — we can flip all traffic to FP16 variant in under 2 minutes and increase capacity on dedicated nodes if needed.

[44:00] Alex Carter: recap: Redwood action items — run 8k calibration, post CSV and updated sheet, enable variant tagging in tracing, add FP8 fallback route to canary policy. Nimble action items — provide 300 golden prompts, anonymized traffic slice, run offline replay for a week. schedule final end-to-end benchmark for 2025-07-18.
[44:30] Jared Mills: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[44:45] Alex Carter: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and share updated sheets. meeting end.
notes: Example transcripts A/B posted in sheet; see tab 'golden-issues'
